steps.title: Open Tapeology
steps.narration: Here's the app's home screen, the live Cockpit. The navigation bar across the top now leads to all three of the product's pages.
steps.point_out: The top nav reads Cockpit, Structure, Desk — the third page, Desk, is what this update is about.

steps.title: Open Structure
steps.narration: Jumping over to the Structure page, where the app maps out a stock's support and resistance levels.
steps.point_out: The Symbol and As-of fields, ready for a lookup.

expect.text: Load a symbol and an as-of time

steps.title: Look up a stock
steps.narration: Typing in a symbol — AAPL — to pull up its price map.

steps.title: Pick a point in time
steps.narration: And a specific moment in time to look at — this is the same pinned example the team uses to prove the chart still works correctly after every change.

steps.title: Load the tradable map
steps.narration: Clicking Load draws the chart and highlights the nearest tradable support/resistance band.
steps.point_out: The candlestick chart and the highlighted price band, right where the team expects it — proof this page still works exactly as before.

steps.title: Open the Desk
steps.narration: Now the page this update is all about: Desk, the operator's daily briefing. It pulls together every stock in the tracked universe into one ranked list.
steps.point_out: The Provenance panel, showing exactly which snapshot of the stock universe and which pricing data this briefing was built from — so anyone can tell two briefings apart or confirm they're identical.

steps.title: See today's ranked briefing
steps.narration: Below the provenance panel sits the actual briefing: every stock with enough price history is ranked by how close it sits to a real support or resistance level.
steps.point_out: Each row shows the side (support or resistance), a letter grade for the level's strength, the distance to it, and a badge for every timeframe of price data behind it.

steps.title: See what got skipped, honestly
steps.narration: Any stock without enough price history isn't hidden or silently dropped — it's listed in its own clearly labeled group, so nothing is quietly missing from the picture.
steps.point_out: The "Skipped" section, grouped by the exact reason each stock couldn't be ranked.
